extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and other USPTO prosecution staff involved in allowance/issue processing
extracted.subtask_short: US patent allowance and issue processing
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for reviewing applications placed in condition for allowance and for preparing them for printing and issuance as U.S. patents, addressed to USPTO examiners and Technology Center staff. Covers final review of disclosure, examiner amendments, drawings, classification/printing choices, withdrawals, quality review, and issuance logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantially Allowable Application, Special
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, except as to matters of form, the application will be considered special and prompt action taken to require correction of formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 710.02(b). Promptly require correction of formal matters; treat as special to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Review of Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is apparently ready for allowance, the examiner should review to make certain the whole application meets all formal and substantive (statutory) requirements and that the language of the claims is enabled by, and finds adequate descriptive support in, the application disclosure as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are enabled and have written description support; confine disclosure to the invention claimed (limit summary/descriptive matter to be in harmony with claims); include sufficient background; check antecedent basis for claim terms; renumber claims per 37 CFR 1.126 and prepare examiner’s amendment if order changed; check abstract (limit 150 words) and title (short and specific); erase any pencil notes; review timeliness of amendments. See MPEP §1302.01, §608.01(c),(d), §608.01(o). Use form paragraphs 13.07 and 13.08 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a Rewritten Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever interlineations or cancellations have been made in the specification or amendments which would lead to confusion and mistake, the examiner should require the entire portion of specification affected to be rewritten before passing the application to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require rewritten portions per 37 CFR 1.125 and MPEP §608.01(q). Use form paragraph 13.01 and specify sections requiring rewrite. See form paragraph guidance and form paragraph 6.28.01 for substitute specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37) Use and Content
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Allowability form PTOL-37 is used whenever an application has been placed in condition for allowance; the date of any communication and/or interview which resulted in the allowance should be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify applicant promptly of allowability both before and after final rejection. If processing delays are expected, notify applicant by interview and mail Interview Summary PTO-413. Prompt notice may avoid unnecessary appeals and abandonment. See MPEP §1302.03 and §714.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Rule on Examiner’s Amendments and Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Except by formal examiner’s amendment duly signed (or as specifically provided), no corrections, erasures, or interlineations may be made in the body of written portions of the specification or any other paper filed in the application for patent (37 CFR 1.121).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal examiner’s amendment for corrections beyond narrowly allowed informal corrections; formal EA must be signed by primary examiner and placed in file with a copy sent to applicant. See MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed Informal Examiner’s Corrections (paper files only)
rubrics_metrics.description: For paper application files an informal examiner’s amendment may be used for correction of obvious errors and omissions (only by the examiner who will initial and assume responsibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of permissible informal corrections: (A) misspelled words; (B) noun-verb disagreement; (C) inconsistent pronoun case; (D) disagreement between reference character in description and drawings (only when certain); (E) entry of Patent No. or Application Publication No. to identify granted/published U.S. application when domestic priority not in ADS; (F) entry of 'abandoned' if referenced U.S. application became abandoned; (G) correction of reversed figure numbers; (H) entry of 'Patent Application No.' for certain older rules; (I) minor grammatical errors; (J) other obvious informalities of purely grammatical nature. Informal EAs not permitted for IFW applications. See MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Adding Parent/Benefit References
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuing applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), an examiner should not add a reference to the prior application without approval of the applicant and a formal examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may decide to delete the priority claim; adding a priority claim may require a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 for unintentionally delayed benefit claim for certain post-Nov 29, 2000 filings. See MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ink and Format Requirements for Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: When correcting originally filed papers of applications with a paper application file wrapper, clean red ink must be used (not blue or black ink).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal corrections are initialed and dated in red ink; formal examiner’s amendments are entered by technical support staff. IFW applications require formal examiner’s amendments for corrections to the body of specification/claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Examiner’s Amendment Use and Form Paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal examiner’s amendment may be used to correct all other informalities in the body of the written portions of the specification as well as all errors and omissions in the claims, but such corrections must be made by formal examiner’s amendment signed by the primary examiner and placed in the file with a copy sent to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal EA should include form paragraph 13.02 and form paragraph 13.02.01. Use form paragraph 13.02.02 if an extension of time is required. Formal EAs are not to be used in reexamination (use form paragraph 22.06). See MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time Required for Certain Examiner’s Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) is required in order to make an examiner’s amendment which places the application in condition for allowance in some situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 13.06 or 13.02.02 where an extension is authorized; when applicant requests extension by telephone, document authorization, duration, deposit account number and fee. See MPEP §706.07(f) item (J) and §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email/Fax Submission for Examiner’s Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment can be created from a facsimile or e-mailed amendment received by the examiner and referenced in the examiner’s amendment and attached thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subject matter to be added in clean version form (no brackets/underlining) should be set forth separately. Print and attach fax/email; mark 'requested' on the entire attachment to avoid term adjustment; attachment becomes part of EA and should be entered in file. Examiners are not required to save emails once printed and entered. E-mail exceptions restricted to e-mails from applicant to examiner and must comply with MPEP §502.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on Examiner Making Substantive Changes Without Applicant Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: No examiner’s amendment, whether formal or informal, may make substantive changes to the written portions of the specification, including the abstract, without obtaining applicant’s approval first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive changes to abstract at time of allowance must be by formal EA and require applicant approval. Courts have noted abstract may determine meaning of claims; examiners should review abstract for compliance with 37 CFR 1.72(b) early in prosecution. See Pandrol USA v. Airboss Railway, Hill-Rom v. Kinetic Concepts, and MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority/Benefit Statements Location Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that an application is a division/continuation/continuation-in-part or claims benefit to an earlier filing should appear as the first sentence of the specification or in an application data sheet (with exceptions for design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps ensure entitlement to earlier U.S. effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. §§120,121,365(c),119(e). If such statements appear elsewhere, relocate or make them in an ADS. CPA practice specifics noted (CPA practice eliminated effective July 14, 2003 for utility/plant). See MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited Not Supplied to Applicant When Passing to Issue
rubrics_metrics.description: References cited as being of interest by examiners when passing an application to issue will not be supplied to applicant; they will be cited on form PTO-892, a copy of which will be attached to the Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References will be indicated on the PTO-892 and printed on the patent as appropriate. See MPEP §1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Slight Drawing Defects Prior to Issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is ready for issue except for a slight defect in the drawing not involving a change in structure, the examiner will prepare a letter indicating the change to be made and, if necessary, include a marked-up copy of the drawing showing the addition or alteration to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §608.02(w). Examiner’s corrections should be clear; necessary EA may be made and copy sent to applicant as attachment to Notice of Allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of Invention Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the title of the invention is not specific to the invention as claimed, the examiner should ensure the title is made specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §606.01. Examiner may change title on or after allowance if applicant has not supplied a satisfactory title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of Obvious Nonstatutory Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a case is otherwise in condition for allowance the examiner may cancel an obviously nonstatutory claim (e.g., 'A device substantially as shown and described').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified of cancellation by an examiner’s amendment. See MPEP §1302.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of Claims to Nonelected or Lost-in-Interference Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims to non-elected inventions or claims lost in an interference should be cancelled as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§821.01–.02 for nonelected invention and §2363.03 for claims lost in interference; handle via examiner’s amendment as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of Rejected Claims Following Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims previously rejected following appeal that should be cancelled when passing to issue must be handled appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§1214.06, 1215.03, and 1215.04 for procedures governing cancellation of such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-to-Date Data for Copending Applications Referred To
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application ready for issue refers by application number to a U.S. nonprovisional application which has matured into a patent, the examiner is authorized to enter the patent number (or 'abandoned' if appropriate) without a formal EA except for IFW applications where a formal EA is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For paper files, entry should be initialed and dated in red ink by the examiner to fix responsibility. If the referred application has become abandoned, enter 'abandoned' in red ink and initial/date. See MPEP §1302.04(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Claims in Examiner’s Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: To identify a claim, a formal examiner’s amendment should refer to it by the original number and, if renumbered in the allowed application, also by the new number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both original and renumbered claim numbers in EAs to avoid ambiguity. See MPEP §1302.04(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Drawings Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application otherwise ready for issue requires correction of the drawing, the application is processed for allowance in the Technology Center and then forwarded to the Publishing Division; any corrected drawings filed by applicant are forwarded to Publishing Division to be matched with the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corrected drawings received are still not acceptable, the Publishing Division will mail a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers' giving a non-extendable period. See MPEP §1302.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement Drawings When Originals Cannot Be Located
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original drawings cannot be located and the application is otherwise in condition for allowance, obtain replacement drawings from Office records of the application as originally filed; require corrected drawings from applicant if reproduced drawings are unacceptable for publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach explanation to Notice of Allowability requiring corrected drawings; if attachment omitted, Publishing Division will mail a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers' with a non-extendable period. See MPEP §1302.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Foreign Application Notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure references to prior foreign applications are handled and noted correctly in preparing application for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§201.14(c) and 202.03 for specific prior foreign application procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Retention Labels to Preserve Abandoned Companion Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a retention label (PTO-150) to preserve related applications referred to in the patent specification from destruction, with the label prepared by technical support staff and applied according to the referenced application's status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions by status: (A) still pending — paste label on face of pending wrapper; (B) abandoned for failure to pay issue fee — send label to Files Repository if forwarded; (C) abandoned — send label to Files Repository or treat as pending; add 'abandoned' in red ink on allowable application; (D) already patented — no label required; add patent number if not present; (E) in issue — fill label and make no change to specification. Only one retention label necessary; add 'et al.' if present. See MPEP §1302.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference Search Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming the application is ready for issue, the examiner makes an interference search and notes the date and class and subclasses searched in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect pending prints and drawings (or claims if invention not susceptible of illustration) in interference files of relevant subclasses and other pertinent classes to ascertain whether any other applicant is claiming substantially the same subject matter. If search discloses no interfering application, prepare application for issue. Note: interference searches may be required in specific TCs (e.g., Working Group 3640). See MPEP §1302.08 and §2301.01(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification, Print Figure, and Other Notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out appropriate spaces on the face of the file wrapper (or Issue Classification sheet for IFW) in black ink; write class and subclass legibly and ensure PALM bib-data is up to date regarding prior applications and priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure numerals and decimal points are distinct; if PALM not updated forward to appropriate office/unit with marked-up copy; ensure class/subclass written in pencil corresponds to issuing class and examiner name. See MPEP §1302.09 and §202.02–.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Claim(s) for Printing in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Select claim(s) to be printed according to defined rules: the broadest claim should be selected; ordinarily designate one claim per invention (up to max five if plurality of inventions); do not select a dependent claim unless the independent claim is also printed; for multiple dependent claims, list entire chain for one embodiment; for reissue select broadest claim with changes or broadest additional reissue claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the claim number(s) on file wrapper in black ink, separated by commas if multiple; use renumbered patent claim number. See MPEP §1302.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for Recording Claim Numbers and Print Figure
rubrics_metrics.description: When recording the selected claim(s) and print figure, write claim number clearly in black ink; separate multiple claims with commas; refer to claim by renumbered patent claim number; select print figure consistent with the claim and not labeled 'prior art'; 'None' may be written if no figure appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily select a single figure consistent with the printed claim; do not select a figure labeled prior art. See MPEP §1302.09.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Classification Notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the appropriate notations in the issuing classification boxes on the face of the file wrapper or on the Issue Classification slip/sheet per classification rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §§903.07, 903.07(b), and 903.09 for notations. For reissue applications include original patent number in the box provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of References for Printing
rubrics_metrics.description: All references cited by the examiner during prosecution (including Board decisions or those listed in a reissue oath) must be listed on either form PTO-892 or on an IDS (PTO/SB/08) and initialed; such reference citations will be printed in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References listed by examiners on PTO-892 are indicated with an asterisk in 'References Cited' on patent front page. Ensure lists are complete and initialed. See MPEP §1302.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal From Issue Procedures (when issue fee paid)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue fee has been paid and the application must be withdrawn from issue, prepare and mail a 'Notice of Withdrawal From Issue under 37 CFR 1.313(b)' and follow additional steps if a patent number and issue date have been assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent number assigned: prepare WDR MEMO, e-mail memorandum to Director of Office of Patent Publication, mail notice no later than Monday before issue date, remove patent number from file wrapper, change application status code (PALM transaction code 1040) to 'Previous Action Withdrawn - Awaiting Further Action', stick Issue Information Label (Form 2016) on file wrapper (not for IFW), forward application to examiner for prompt action (reopen prosecution, initiate interference). See MPEP §1308.01 and §1308.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection After Allowance and Withdrawal for New Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only with approval of the primary examiner. If a new reference is discovered that clearly applies to allowed claims, a memorandum is addressed to the TC Director requesting withdrawal from issue to apply the new reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorandum should cite the reference and briefly state its application; submit with reference and file wrapper (if paper). If request approved, TC Director withdraws application and examiner issues an Office action rejecting claims in view of the new reference. If issue fee paid and prosecution reopened applicant may request refund or credit or wait to see outcome. See MPEP §1308.01–.02 and §706.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Review Program for Examined Patent Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Quality Assurance administers a program reviewing the quality of examination of patent applications via randomly selected samples of allowed applications from each examiner, reviewed by Review Quality Assurance Specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review may include independent search; excludes applications with Board or court decisions. The reviewer may consult others (not the original examiner). Reviewed applications may be returned to TCs for consideration; if claims are determined unpatentable prosecution is reopened with form paragraph 13.04. Quality Assurance forms/papers are not to be included with Office actions or retained in the file; do not indicate in the record that QA review was conducted. See MPEP §1308.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopen Prosecution - After Notice of Allowance (Form Paragraph 13.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a previously allowed claim is considered unpatentable after the Notice of Allowance, use form paragraph 13.04 to reopen prosecution and state appropriate rejections for each claim considered unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket 1: identify claim(s) considered unpatentable; Bracket 2: state all appropriate rejections. If issue fee paid, additional steps (form paragraph 13.05) are required. See MPEP §1308.03 and form paragraph 13.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacate Notice of Allowance (Form Paragraph 13.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is reopened after mailing of the Notice of Allowance, use form paragraph 13.05 to vacate the Notice of Allowance and advise applicant regarding refund or credit of issue fee or awaiting allowance/abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert date of Notice of Allowance in bracket. Explain options for refund/credit if issue fee paid; applicant may wait until application is allowed or held abandoned and then request fee treatment accordingly. See MPEP §1308.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue of Patent - Data Capture and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under current publication process, electronic capture of information to be printed begins as soon as an allowed application is received in the Office of Patent Publication; Initial Data Capture (IDC) takes approximately five weeks, during which the paper application is not available; after Final Data Capture and final issue preparation the application is assigned a patent number and issue date about ten days before issuance and Issue Notification is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed applications are forwarded to printer for IDC; after IDC application returned to Office of Patent Publication and then to printer for Final Data Capture (FDC) upon payment of issue fee and fulfillment of other requirements; ensure drawings and other requirements met within time allowed by law. See MPEP §1309.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Handling Categories for Issuance Scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications ready for printing will be selected by chronological sequence based on date the issue fee was paid, with special handling for certain categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special categories: (A) cases made special by Director (including Special Examining Procedure); (B) U.S. effective filing date more than 5 years old; (C) allowed reissue applications; (D) allowed applications having effective filing date earlier than that required for declaring an interference; (E) allowed application of a party involved in a terminated interference. Examiner should contact Image Assistance Center for special treatment if application falls into these categories. See MPEP §1309.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing Names of Practitioners and Firms on Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fee(s) Transmittal form provides space for the person submitting the base issue fee to indicate names of up to three registered practitioners or alternatively the name of a single firm (with up to two practitioner names) to be printed on the patent; leaving blank results in no practitioner/firm printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If person submitting issue fee desires no name printed, leave space blank. If filled out, those names will be printed on the patent. See MPEP §1309 (Printing names section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Printed on Patent - PTOL-85B Item 3
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fee(s) Transmittal form portion (PTOL-85B) of the Notice of Allowance provides a space for assignment data which should be completed to comply with 37 CFR 3.81; unless assignee name/address identified, the patent will issue to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment data printed on the patent is based solely on information supplied on PTOL-85B. Recording of the assignment (submission for recordation) as set forth in 37 CFR 3.11 is required for a patent to issue to an assignee; see MPEP §307 and 37 CFR 3.81(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee Names Printing Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the first appearing name of an assignee will be printed on the patent where multiple names for the same party are identified on PTOL-85B (e.g., legal name and d.b.a.), although assignment recording practice is unaffected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete PTOL-85B assignee entry to indicate assignment data as recorded in the Office; printed patent will show first appearing name. See MPEP §1309.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling 'Query/Printer Waiting' Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When the printer finds an apparent error it returns the file with an attached 'Query/Printer Waiting' slip; the application should be acted on immediately and returned within 72 hours (excluding weekends/holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take corrective action or indicate application is correct; enter a copy of the query in the file; if concurred in criticisms, correct in clean red ink and initial or correct by examiner’s amendment (IFW requires formal EA). Delays may be avoided by telephoning applicant and correcting by amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 where appropriate. Do not mail such applications to Publishing Division; follow IFW-specific process for IFW apps. See MPEP §1309.02.
